content:
ashley: Heads up — saw a reproducible perf spike in canary today when the kernel picker chooses FP8 attention + INT8 FF on SM92 for long-streaming runs (seq > 4k). p95 jumped ~60ms and memcpy stalls look suspicious. attaching profiler snippet below.

ashley: repro: mixed-quant inference, streaming tokens, 8-token bursts, kv_cache chunking enabled. observed on dedicated pool.

tomas: Do you have the kernel names? My guess is it picked `fp8_attn_v2` + `int8_ff_v1` which used different workspace layout and triggered extra host-device copies during KV stitching.

ashley: profiler timeline:
```
attn_kernel(fp8_attn_v2):   3.4ms
memcpy(kv_chunk_merge):      7.1ms  <-- big
ff_kernel(int8_ff_v1):       2.0ms
overlap stalls:              45ms  (waiting on kv memcpy)
```

liam: Oof. That memcpy number suggests stripe/chunking interactions — KV packing for fp8 path expects contiguous layout, but int8 path writes into a different stride. When we switch kernels mid-layer we may be doing a transpose/copy per chunk.

sasha: Could be the autotuner's seqlen_thresholds are too low for FP8 winning. Currently FP8 seqlen_threshold is 2048 for SM92 in the table. If the model does bursty long seqs we should raise it or add a transition penalty for quant-mixed paths.

tomas: Proposed quick experiments:
- force attn -> int8 (disable fp8_attn_v2) to see baseline
- bump `seqlen_threshold_fp8` to 8192 for SM92
- try `kv_warmup_ratio=0.25` to reduce chunk merges during early streaming

ashley: Agreed. Also want to try a configuration knob: `quant_transition_penalty` (float) applied when adjacent layers use different quant families — treat it like an additive latency in the tuner so picks prefer uniform quantization unless benefit > penalty.

liam: Matches my thinking. We should add that to the autotuner AND add telemetry to record if transition penalty prevented a pick (so we can roll back if it hurts quality).

perf-bot: Dashboard: https://perf.internal/runs/2079/canary/kv-thrash-2079998887 (charts for p50/p95, memcpy timings, kernel picks)

ashley: Autotune command I'm going to run locally:
```
./tools/autotune \
  --model llama-70b \
  --arch sm92 \
  --quant int8,fp8 \
  --seq-buckets 512,1024,2048,4096,8192 \
  --override seqlen_threshold_fp8=8192 \
  --override kv_warmup_ratio=0.25 \
  --override quant_transition_penalty=1.5
```

tomas: I'll run the canary with `--tidy 10%` and the rollout policy: 10% for 2h, auto-fallback to int8-only if p95 > baseline+p95_thresh(20ms).

sasha: Reminder: also run `scripts/eval-quant-shift.py --promptset smoke` to sanity-check output drift when forcing int8 vs fp8. FP8 rounding can change logits in subtle ways. We need a small eval harness and a KV correctness test for chunk boundaries.

liam: I'll add a quick unit test for kv chunk merge invariants and a microbench that toggles stripe_size from 64..512 to see memcpy curve. Expect memcpy cliff when stripe misaligns with warp-aligned layout.

ashley: Action items:
- tomas: run autotune + canary with overrides above (owner)
- liam: add kv chunking unit test + stripe microbench (owner)
- sasha: run eval-quant-shift smoke and add telemetry for transition_penalty (owner)
- ashley: collect perf traces and update tuner table if results are stable after 24h

ashley: tagging this as high priority for today's perf triage. ping me on thread when canary results are in. :eyes:

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary rollout (10%) for pool redwood-sm92-canary at 2079999000 (eta ~2m).

tomas: starting runs now, will paste logs back here.

ashley: thanks — if anyone sees correctness blips, abort canary immediately.
